name: Primary Cutaneous Plasmacytosis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: No standardized formal criteria; diagnosis based on clinical and histopathological findings

criteria.description: Presence of multiple reddish-brown to violaceous macules, papules, or plaques predominantly on the trunk
Dense dermal infiltrate of mature polyclonal plasma cells without evidence of malignancy
Absence of systemic plasmacytosis or plasma cell neoplasm confirmed by clinical and laboratory evaluation
Polyclonal expression of immunoglobulin light chains (kappa and lambda) in plasma cells
Normal or mildly elevated polyclonal gammopathy without monoclonal spike

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met: characteristic cutaneous lesions, histopathologic confirmation of polyclonal plasma cell infiltrate, and exclusion of systemic disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires careful exclusion of systemic plasmacytosis and plasma cell malignancies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple reddish-brown to violaceous macules and papules on the trunk
searchTerms: small red to purple bumps on body
many colored skin spots on torso

pathognomonic.symptomName: Dense dermal infiltrate of mature polyclonal plasma cells on skin biopsy
searchTerms: skin biopsy showing many plasma cells
dense immune cell buildup in skin sample
skin tissue with lots of plasma cells

common.symptomName: Pruritus localized to affected skin areas

searchTerms: mild increase in blood immune proteins
red skin patches with light flakes
no or small swollen lymph nodes
absent or slight lymph node swelling

occasional.symptomName: Mild constitutional symptoms such as low-grade fever
searchTerms: mild general symptoms like low-grade fever

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss

searchTerms: spread of plasma cell disease throughout body

laboratory: Polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia on serum protein electrophoresis
imaging: No specific imaging findings; imaging used to exclude systemic involvement
other: Skin biopsy showing dense dermal plasma cell infiltrate with polyclonal immunoglobulin expression

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic involvement with lymphadenopathy and organomegaly
Polyclonal plasma cell infiltration in multiple organs
Presence of systemic myeloma features such as bone lesions
Monoclonal protein spike on serum electrophoresis

redFlags: Development of systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, or night sweats
Presence of monoclonal gammopathy or bone lesions
references: Watanabe T, et al. Primary cutaneous plasmacytosis: a clinicopathologic study of 10 cases. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2015.
Kawachi Y, et al. Cutaneous plasmacytosis: a review of 21 cases. J Dermatol. 2017.
